comments.anchorText: Hanc deus et melior litem natura diremit.
comments.body: Line 24. Both Deus ("quisquis deum..." whoever of the gods it was...) and melior natura (nature meaning natural processes; melior meaning better than the chaos that came before) are what assembled the world. Thus the Stoics who demanded a Demiurge were satisfied, and the Epicureans too, who said it was Nature. Ovid had it both ways.
Line 4. fert here with definition 10 from wiktionary, to incite, to impel, to move
Line 25. 3rd indic. act. perfect tense. Cut away (with an instrument). Figuratively, banish, separate, expel.
